Question 20 of 20, Level 3

20Case studyCBSE SQP 2025-264 marks
Case Study: LED bulbs are energy-efficient because they use much less electricity than traditional bulbs while producing the same amount of light. A company manufactures a new type of energy-efficient LED bulb. The cost of production and the revenue generated by selling xxx bulbs (in an hour) are modelled as C(x)=0.5x2−10x+150C(x) = 0.5x^2 - 10x + 150C(x)=0.5x2−10x+150 and R(x)=−0.3x2+20xR(x) = -0.3x^2 + 20xR(x)=−0.3x2+20x respectively, where C(x)C(x)C(x) and R(x)R(x)R(x) are both in ₹. Use the given models to answer the following questions.
  1. (i)Derive the profit function P(x)P(x)P(x).1 mark
  2. (ii)Find the critical points of P(x)P(x)P(x).1 mark
  3. (iii)(a)Determine whether the critical points correspond to a maximum or a minimum profit by using the second derivative test.2 marks
  4. OR
  5. (iii)(b)Identify the possible practical value of xxx (i.e. the number of bulbs that can realistically be produced and sold) that can maximise the profit, if the resources available and the expenditure on machines allow the company to produce a minimum of 10 but not more than 18 bulbs per hour. Also calculate the maximum profit.2 marks

Work it out on paper first. Then reveal the solution one step at a time.

Formula / idea Profit === Revenue −-− Cost; P′(x)=0P'(x) = 0P′(x)=0 gives critical points; P′′(x)<0P''(x) < 0P′′(x)<0 gives a maximum.

(i)1 mark

Answer (i)P(x)=−0.8x2+30x−150\displaystyle P(x) = -0.8x^2 + 30x - 150P(x)=−0.8x2+30x−150
